_about: Choreography styles, chain plans, telegraphs and beam-clash shapes (Combat). Design: docs/combat/variety-pass.md. Templates stay the judge (outcome, tags, selector draws); a style only changes how the chosen branch looks, as an overlay on its 'dynamic' beats. Not read by the sim until Encounter's style slice. Numbers marked 'suggestion' are Game Design's to set. Schema: tools/schemas/combat-styles.schema.json (Tools).

altitudeBands._note: height above the local surface (groundY, or sea level over water), read at exchange start

mood._note: Game Design's fight mood (spec-wounds.md section 9): a director value 0 to 100

act._note: 1 + region breaks + transformations (both fighters), capped at 4 (spec-wounds.md section 9)

traits._note: per fighter; moves to the roster data (D1) when it lands. Placeholders now, archetypes later.
traits._held: The blink trait has no effect while teleporting is on hold (the blink_clash style has weight 0).

tempo._note: ticks, added to profiles.dynamic.tempo for styled beats. Suggestions.

telegraphs._about: Players now play by reads (questionnaire 4, stance-matrix.md R9): every exchange shows the attacker's weight, and every finisher shows its kind, in-world as well as on the stance ring.

light.at: the first beat of the approach
light.look: a quick guard-up bounce, a small aura spark

heavy.at: the first beat of the approach
heavy.look: a coil, a glowing fist, a heavier aura

sig.look: the charge orb and the name banner, 0.8 s

weight._rule: Driven by the existing 'attack' fx event, which carries the attack kind at the start of every exchange: Rendering shows tell_light or tell_heavy on the attacker for the whole approach (every template's approach starts at tick 0). No data beat is needed, so the tell is in every profile. Blink approaches show it at the first blink_out.

finishers._rule: each finisher's kind lives on the finisher (finishers.json 'kind': launch, melee or beam). Encounter adds it to finisher_start, and Rendering shows finisher_tell_<kind> with the finisher_open cue, so the fighter on the brink can read it (spec-wounds.md section 1: DEFENSIVE against launch, EVASIVE against melee, AGGRESSIVE with 40 ki or more against beam)

struggle._rule: resolved by state and drawn once at contestOpen (finishers.json contest.struggle.byState). The three pulses at beatTicks (18, 36, 54) emit struggle_pulse (holding or slipping) and cue struggle_hold or struggle_slip; the sequence reveals the drawn result step by step with no further draw.

parry._rule: R5: a director roll resolved by state in the four parryable templates. The wind beat stays as the visible tell (with the weight cue), and a successful parry plays its flash and the clean-parry cue on the parryable strike. No press, no window input.

heavy_clash._rule: the prelude replaces the approach and footwork; the branch's decider (strike or clashWave) lands at deciderAt, its wind (WON only) at deciderAt - heavyWindup, and every later beat of the branch shifts by the same amount

trade_blows._rule: each exchanged blow lands at a new blink position, 4 ticks after the pair reappears; the decider stays where the dynamic profile puts it

styles._held: Teleporting is on hold (Orb, 2026-10-01): base weight 0 switches this style off. The factors and the overlay are kept for when it returns; it may become one character's signature ability.

approach._rule: no rush: the attacker fires from where it stands

overlay._rule: each of PRESSURE's three strikes becomes two blasts carrying half its damage into the raised guard (stance multiplier applies as today); the guard shove and the chain window follow as in the dynamic profile

the approach still closes (pillar 3): the blasts fly while the attacker rushes in. result byBranch: land on an attacker-favoured branch, guard against DEFENSIVE, evade on a defender or neutral branch. 3 blasts at 4 damage (12 in all), stance multipliers apply, normal 4% ki gain; the contemptuous poke (a volley-trait fighter at 700 u or more) uses the same 3 at 4 (Game Design, balance-targets.md section 12)

chains._about: Cleaner combos: a chain is a phrase with an opener (the exchange's own launch), links on a fixed rhythm and always one ender. The director decides at each window with one draw against chainP (Encounter's Q4 plan: it replaces the attacker's press). Suggestions for Game Design.

blitz._rule: decided at the first window when a chain starts: a blitz is a fast chain of at least minLinks links at blitzGap instead of linkGap (later windows force 'continue' until minLinks). Game Design tunes the chance toward 2 to 6 blitzes a minute in Tense and Frenzied.

link._note: a small pop that keeps the body near: links juggle, only the ender sends it away

cadence._rule: each link starts linkGap (or blitzGap) ticks after the previous one starts, with no press delay; after the ender no window opens

chainP._rule: p = clamp(byStance[stance][mood] + perComboAbove1 * (combo - 1) + heat[stage], floor, cap), and 0 when ki < minKi. The heat bonus is for fighters with the heat track only (stance-matrix.md R9). First window: continue if draw < p, else no chain. Later windows: continue with a link if draw < p and combo + 1 < capHits, else play the ender. Under ADR 0008 the queued presses set the links for human players; chainP is the AI's and the Simple layout's policy.
chainP._source: Game Design, balance-targets.md section 12: slightly below the suggestion to hold the chain band (15 to 35 per 100 melee exchanges)

beamClash._about: Six clash shapes, chosen from the margin between the two clash scores the code already draws (no new draws) plus position and mood. First match in this order wins.

deflect._note: the loser pays 20 ki, is pushed back 700 and takes no damage; a deflect into a settlement is a set piece under the collateral budgets (Game Design, balance-targets.md section 12, section 4b)

split._note: chip damage 40 to each fighter, ignoring stance (Game Design, balance-targets.md section 12)

mutual._note: chip damage 60 to each fighter, ignoring stance, launched apart at 1,400 (Game Design, balance-targets.md section 12)

actWeight._rule: higher acts favour the long shapes: at act 3 or more, a margin in the overpower band plays as a seesaw 40% of the time (composition-stream draw)

rule._note: templates.json beam.outcome: CLASH when the defender is AGGRESSIVE with 40 ki or more (state, no draw). R9 answer 2 keeps it; the ambush clause only matters for the future stealth fighter.

meter.byFighter: roster data (F1): each fighter's own ego meter (Pride, Wrath, Hunger, Respect) * 0.08

score._rule: score = tier*10 + ki*0.35 + S.rng.range_(0, 16) + meter term; one draw per fighter, attacker first (beam.gd today). margin = |score(A) - score(D)| picks the shape; the winner is the higher score. The dynamic profile reads these numbers; parity keeps the code's
